semis.why: 18/18 names bid pre-market (median +2.1%, SOXX +1.5%) from an oversold base (5d -5.6%, median 1% below the 50d, RSIs 30s-40s) on real news: SK hynix union ratified the wage deal (Bloomberg Sep 16), KOSPI +1.4%, Soitec +11.5% (driver unverified). Hike almost fully priced, so the priced decision should not undo the lead.

big_tech.why: Most extended group (median +8.6% vs 50d, META RSI 72) into a 10Y at 5.0%; no pre-market bid of its own (+0.1% median); rotation into oversold chips comes at its expense.

ai_power_infra.why: All four bid pre-market (AIXA +4.1%, BE +3.5%), group 12% below its 50d, oil -2.3%; the most beaten group in a relief tape.

sg_banks.why: STI flattened at 5,638 after a 1.6% week, banks marginally bid today (+0.2% median); a priced hike does not change their rate picture. Next SGX close is after the Fed.

market.why: Chips up and big tech soft offset in the index; the hike is priced and the post-14:00 ET leg (dots + presser) is a genuine coin flip.

summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have. Chips are bouncing from an oversold base on real news, but the Fed decides at 2am SGT with the 10-year at 5%, and that sets the close. Don't add anything before the press conference.
summary.where_we_are: Wednesday 19:50 SGT / 07:50 ET. US pre-market, cash opens 21:30 SGT. SGX closed, STI flat at 5,638. Next: US retail sales 20:30 SGT, then the Fed decision with projections at 02:00 SGT Thursday and the press conference at 02:30 SGT. The Bank of Japan meets Thursday and Friday.
summary.macro_attribution: Since Tuesday's close oil has moved most: WTI is off 2.3% to $103 on a surprise 7.1-million-barrel US crude build (CNBC summary, Sep 16), gold is up 1.2%, the 10-year is unchanged at 5.0% and VIX is down 2% at 16.9 (tape). The lean depends on the Fed calendar, not on oil; the oil drop is a mild tailwind and is not load-bearing.
what_happened: All 18 chip names are up pre-market, median +2.1%, SOXX +1.5% (tape). It follows a 5.6% five-session drop that left the group 1% below its 50-day with RSIs in the 30s to 40s: a rebound from below, not an extension. Pre-market bars carry no volume, so the bid is thin until the cash session confirms it.

SK Hynix, the memory leader, rose 4.1% in Seoul and the KOSPI 1.4% (tape) after 57% of its union ratified the revised wage deal paying half of bonuses in cash (Bloomberg, Sep 16). The strike overhang is gone.

Soitec, which makes the wafers under silicon-photonics chips, is up 11.5% in Paris (tape). The search returns an investing.com piece on a photonics guidance raise, but its price levels do not match today's tape, so today's driver is unverified. Nokia +5.8% and Tower +4.1% pre-market, reasons not found.

A quarter-point Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% is almost fully priced and a further October hike is near a coin flip (CME FedWatch via CNBC live blog summary, Sep 16). The 10-year is hovering above 5% (CNBC, Sep 16). Strategists at Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan and Goldman say dips on tightening will be short-lived (Bloomberg, Sep 14); a hiking-cycle start has historically cost the S&P 3.4% in the following month (Bloomberg summary, Sep 14).
Big tech is flat pre-market and sits 8.6% above its 50-day with Meta's RSI at 72 (tape): the extended group facing a 5% ten-year.

per_group.semis: slightly up. An oversold group getting fundamental news (Hynix labor resolved, Asia bid) with the hike already priced; the pre-market lead should survive a priced decision. Memory and equipment lead; the GPU clouds (CoreWeave, Nebius) are following at +2%, not leading.
per_group.big_tech: slightly down. The most extended group into a 5% ten-year, no pre-market bid of its own, and the rotation into chips comes at its expense.
per_group.ai_power_infra: slightly up. Twelve percent below its 50-day, all four bid pre-market (Aixtron +4.1%, Bloom +3.5%) and oil is off: the most beaten group in a relief tape.
per_group.sg_banks: flat. The index has flattened at 5,638 after a 1.6% week, the banks are marginally bid today, and a priced hike does not change their rate picture.
per_group.market: flat. Chips up and big tech soft offset in the index, and the leg after 2am is a genuine coin flip.

change_my_mind: The cash open fades the chip bid on volume, with SOXX back below Tuesday's close by 22:30 SGT: chips flip to flat or down, the pre-market was thin.
The dots show two or more further hikes or the press conference is hawkish and the 10-year goes through 5.05%: everything flips down, big tech worst.
Retail sales at 20:30 SGT come in far above the +0.8% consensus: the 10-year rises before the Fed and the chip lean weakens.
The 10-year falls after the press conference: big tech and the whole market flip to up.
summary.confidence: the decision at 02:00 SGT is the whole session and only the hike itself is knowable; the dots and the tone are not.
summary.cant_know: The dot plot and the press-conference tone, which set the last two hours of the session.
summary.the_call: Up in chips, flat in the index. Chips gain moderately, about 1%, led by memory and equipment; big tech is the laggard and slips mildly; the whole market closes near flat as the two offset until the Fed speaks.
